technology_name: Anoxic-Oxic Sequential Batch Biofilm Reactor: Wastewater Treatment System
institution: KSCSTE- Centre for Water Resources Development and Management (CWRDM)
problem_solved: Conventional Sequencing Batch Reactors (SBRs) for treating high-strength slaughterhouse wastewater suffer from high sludge production and poor settling (high sludge volume index).
description: This innovation is an Anoxic-Oxic Sequential Batch Biofilm Reactor (SBBR) that incorporates inert carrier materials into a conventional SBR system to support biofilm growth. This design combines suspended and attached growth systems to simultaneous remove carbonaceous organic matter and nutrients from high-strength slaughterhouse wastewater. Operating under phased oxygen conditions (aerobic/anoxic react combinations), the system optimizes microbial biomass accumulation and accelerates organic matter decomposition without excessive sludge production.
applications:
• Treatment of high-BOD and nutrient-rich wastewater from commercial slaughterhouses and meat processing units

• Upgrading existing municipal or industrial wastewater treatment plants to biofilm-based systems

• Decentralized sanitation and effluent treatment in resource-limited or space-constrained settings

• Effluent compliance management for food and beverage industry processing facilities
secondary_sector: Energy, Climate & Sustainability, Biotechnology & Life Sciences, Food Technology
